thread:
runtime-detector: ALERT: initContainer in pod cache-redis-7bb2 mounted host /proc and wrote to /host/proc/sysrq-trigger (score=0.94)

maria-ops: seeing this on the security feed. node ip-10-1-3-88. init container shows privileged: true and hostPID: true. please isolate the node.

jeff-sec: @maria-ops ack. cordon the node and please snapshot the pod before killing.

tamika-platform: on it. `kubectl cordon ip-10-1-3-88` then `kubectl -n prod get pods -o wide | grep ip-10-1-3-88`

sergio-runtime: grab pod yaml, image digest, and a process list from the container. `kubectl -n prod get pod cache-redis-7bb2 -o yaml > /tmp/pod.yaml` and `kubectl -n prod exec -it cache-redis-7bb2 -- ps aux`

maria-ops: copied pod yaml, container logs, and kubelet journal to /tmp and uploaded to s3. kernel logs show execve events and a write to /host/proc/sysrq-trigger around 16:00.

jeff-sec: execve + sysrq write lines up with a binary trying to interact with host proc. could be a tampered image pushed by CI. treat as potential compromise.

oncall-eric: node cordoned and pod terminated at 16:02. captured container filesystem with `crictl snapshot` and tarred artifacts to s3://redwood-forensics/1876543210/ forensics/

sara-sre: pulled image manifest and ran `skopeo inspect`. `cosign verify` failed — no signatures found. registry shows a push ~1 hour before the alert from serviceaccount ci-deployer.

tamika-platform: emergency actions: blocked the offending digest at the admission webhook, rotated the registry push token used by ci-deployer, and removed cluster-admin from that SA.

sergio-runtime: found a script in the image layer: `/usr/local/bin/host-mount.sh` that does `mount --bind /proc /host/proc && echo b > /host/proc/sysrq-trigger`. saved a copy to artifacts.

maria-ops: opened PagerDuty incident 18765 and alerted security@redwood. created GH issue in infra-policy for denying hostProc in initContainers and adding audit checks.

jeff-sec: follow-ups: 1) add audit rule to log pods/initContainers with hostPID/hostIPC/privileged=true and any host mounts; 2) enforce PodSecurityPolicy/PodSecurity admission to deny hostProc/hostPID for initContainers; 3) require cosign signatures for images in CI and verify in admission webhook; 4) search cluster for similar activity.

tamika-platform: short-term: admission webhook to reject unsigned images and a registry IP blocklist. long-term: integrate cosign signing with our KMS-managed keys and rotate CI signing credentials.

sara-sre: do not rotate KMS keys yet unless we find key exposure. rotate registry tokens and node kubelet certs, and revoke any service account tokens that had push rights.

sergio-runtime: forensics will scan for outbound connections and lateral movement between 15:45-16:05 across all nodes and check kubelet logs for similar mounts.

maria-ops: adding post-incident tasks to the incident board: admission webhook enforcement, RBAC tightening for CI, audit logging rules, cosign enforcement in CI, periodic image integrity scans, and update runbook.

runtime-detector: RULE UPDATE: new signature to flag initContainers that bind-mount /proc to /host/proc and write to sysctl paths. tuning applied to reduce false positives.

jeff-sec: interim thread closing — we'll do a formal postmortem after the forensics report is in. thanks everyone for the quick response.
